answer: In an agent marketplace for meadow seed, nectar, and lotus bulbs, each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days to receive a quota of ten bids per hour. Creating more identities does not create free bidding capacity: every additional quota requires another bond. An attacker seeking 10,000 bids per hour must immobilize 100,000 tokens, bearing financing costs and losing access to that capital for the full lock period.
